subject: MATH
title: Calculus I
description: Differentiation, curve sketching, maximum-minimum problems, related rates, mean-value theorem, antiderivative, Riemann integral, logarithm, and exponential functions.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 121 or appropriate performance on the department placement test.

subject: CS
title: CS 111 or CS 112 or CS 113 (Program Design I)
description: A first programming course: variables, data types, control structures, functions, and simple data structures, taught in a high-level language. Students write many small programs. Some universities offer versions set in a particular field, such as biology or law.
notes: Student chooses one: Program Design I | Program Design I in the Context of Biological Problems | Program Design I in the Context of Law and Public Policy.

subject: ENGL
title: Academic Writing I: Writing in Academic and Public Contexts
description: Students write in a variety of genres with an emphasis on argument and sentence-level grammar. Topics vary by section.
prerequisites: Eligibility as determined by performance on the Department placement test.

title: Science Elective
description: A laboratory science course chosen from an approved list, such as biology, chemistry, or physics, usually with a lecture and a lab. These courses introduce scientific methods and the main ideas of the field.
notes: UIC: select two courses (8 hours) from the approved list (e.g. BIOS 110, CHEM 122/123, PHYS 141).

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Success Seminar for Freshmen
description: A general orientation course on skills pertinent to students for successful completion of their undergraduate degree.
notes: UIC: ENGR 100 is a one-semester-hour course, but the hour does not count toward the total hours required for graduation (counts_toward_total = false). Transfer students take ENGR 101.
prerequisites: Admission to the College of Engineering. Degree-seeking students only.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus II
description: Techniques of integration, arc length, solids of revolution, applications, polar coordinates, parametric equations, infinite sequences and series, power series.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 180.

subject: ENGL
title: Academic Writing II: Writing for Inquiry and Research
description: Students learn about academic inquiry and complete several writing projects including a documented research paper. Topics vary by section.
prerequisites: ENGL 160 or the equivalent. All students take the Writing Placement test except for those with test-based exemptions noted here. If students place into ENGL 060, ENGL 070, ENGL 071, and ENGL 160, the student must take the course (or courses) prior to enrolling in ENGL 161. Students with an ACT English subscore of 27 or higher, SAT Evidence-Based Critical Reading score of 630 or higher, AP English Language & Composition score of 3 or higher, or IB English Language A: Language & Literature score of 6 or higher, receive credit for ENGL 160 and permission to enroll in ENGL 161.

title: General Education Core course
description: A general education course outside the major, chosen from an approved list in one of several breadth categories, such as world cultures, the creative arts, history, or society. These courses develop critical thinking, communication, and an understanding of society and culture.
notes: UIC requires one course in each of five categories: Exploring World Cultures, Understanding the Creative Arts, Understanding the Past, Understanding the Individual and Society, Understanding U.S. Society. The schedule doesn't say which goes where.

subject: CS
title: Program Design II
description: Data abstraction and modular design; recursion; lists and stacks; dynamic memory allocation; file manipulation; programming exercises.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 111 or Grade of C or better in CS 112 or Grade of C or better in CS 113 or Grade of C or better in CS 107 or Grade of C or better in CS 109; and Credit or concurrent registration in MATH 180.

subject: CS
title: Mathematical Foundations of Computing
description: Discrete mathematics concepts fundamental to computing: propositional logic, predicates and quantifiers; proofs; sets; recursive definitions and induction; functions, relations and graphs; combinatorics and discrete probability; applications.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 111 or Grade of C or better in CS 112 or Grade of C or better in CS 113 or Grade of C or better in CS 107 or Grade of C or better in CS 109 or Grade of C or better in MCS 160; and Credit or concurrent registration in MATH 180; or appropriate score on the department placement test Note that a grade of C in MCS 260 (the prior course number for MCS 160) is also considered a valid prerequisite replacement for MCS 160.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus III
description: Vectors in space, functions of several variables, partial differential and optimization, multiple integrals, vector fields, Green’s Theorem, Stokes Theorem.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 181.

subject: CS
title: Programming Practicum
description: Software development tools and practices; debugging and testing; advanced language features; standard libraries; code management.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 141; or Grade of C or better in CS 107. The option to use CS 107 as a prerequisite (in place of CS 141) is only for Computer Engineering majors or students doing a Computer Engineering minor.

subject: CS
title: Data Structures
description: Design, usage and analysis of data structures: review of lists, stacks and queues; hash tables, priority queues, search trees, introduction to graphs; searching and sorting; runtime analysis; programming projects and lab exercises.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 141 or Grade of C or better in CS 107; and Grade of C or better in CS 151; and Credit or concurrent registration in CS 211 or Credit or concurrent registration in ECE 266.

subject: CS
title: Machine Organization
description: Data representation and computer arithmetic; machine language; addressing; memory hierarchy; subroutines; data structures; processor architecture: hardware components, pipelining.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 141; and Credit or concurrent registration in CS 211.

subject: CS
title: Languages and Automata
description: Regular sets and finite automata. Context-free languages and push-down automata. Parsing. Computability theory including Turing machines and decidability.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 151; and Credit or concurrent registration in CS 251.

title: Required Mathematics course
description: An additional mathematics or statistics course chosen from an approved list. Typical choices include probability and statistics, linear algebra, numerical analysis, and discrete mathematics.
notes: UIC: 9 hours from an approved list, including at least one of IE 342 or STAT 381.

title: Humanities/Social Sciences/Art Elective
description: A course in the humanities, social sciences, or arts chosen by the student from a broad approved list. These courses add breadth outside engineering and computing.

subject: CS
title: Systems Programming
description: Study of computer systems emphasizing impact on application level programming. Virtual memory and memory management; code optimization; system-level I/O; concurrency: processes, threads, synchronization; introduction to network programming.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 251 and Grade of C or better in CS 211; and CS 261.

subject: CS
title: Computer Design
description: Computer hardware building blocks. logic gates; combinational circuits; arithmetic circuits; flip flops and sequential circuits; registers and memory; CPU design; I/O design.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 211; and CS 261.

subject: CS
title: Software Design
description: Software design principles and practices: Object-oriented design; design patterns; software reuse; testing; event driven programming and concurrency; graphical user interface design and development; Team development.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 251 and Grade of C or better in CS 211.

title: Technical and Professional Communication in Computer Science
description: Communication skills for computing students and professionals in various contexts: technical writing, portfolios, job interviews, demos, sales, with speech organization, visuals, and delivery. Attendance, participation, and presentations required.

subject: CS
title: Programming Language Design and Implementation
description: Programming language paradigms, design and implementation: syntax and semantics; parsing; runtime systems; control; data types; subroutines and exceptions; data and procedural abstraction; functional programming.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in CS 211 and Grade of C or better in CS 251.

subject: CS
title: Ethical Issues in Computing
description: Ethical and social issues in computing: privacy and surveillance, social media and society, technology and economic inequality, technology-related intellectual property law, professional ethics.
prerequisites: CS 277 and Credit or concurrent registration in CS 251; or approval of the department.

subject: CS
title: Computer Algorithms I
description: Design and analysis of computer algorithms. Divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy method, backtracking. Algorithms for sorting, searching, graph computations, pattern matching, NP-complete problems.
prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MCS 360; or Grade of C or better in CS 251.
